analysis.title: Connecting You to GS.. Thoughts from the Floor
key_insights: Goldman's trading desks read the post-CPI Fed repricing as a hiking cycle. GS Economics now expects a third 25bp hike in March after September and December and does not rule out January. The desks agree a 50bp December hike (Waller's call) is unlikely, with only 27 priced.

Desk views on the terminal rate differ. Korapaty (USD Rates Vol) puts the end of the current adjustment at 4.25-4.5% with neutral at 3.75-4%. Xholi (US Swaps) says the market prices a peak around 4.75% by next fall, which he sees as above where the Committee ends up, and calls U7 a buy. Bingham expects hikes to be front-loaded into Q1 2027 and prefers receiving structures.

Inflation has surprised to the upside over the last 3-4 months with no single category driving it. Lavenberg tracks core MoM about 10bps above consensus in each of the last two months. The outcome depends on shelter: a 30bps OER run rate versus 20bps would put a floor under early-2027 inflation, while a reversion to baseline shelter trend keeps reinflation risk muted.

Walker (US Economics) says the October CPI printed 30bp even though noisy components (airfares, health insurance, used cars) fell. He moves his November and December core run rate from mid-teens to high teens or low 20s, and says the data makes it harder to fully embrace the transitory view.

Cahill (FX Strategy) sees further near-term dollar strength, particularly against G10, because policy tightening is happening while energy falls but other inflation pressures persist. He is watching whether US tightening exposes the European vulnerabilities seen earlier in the year.

European inflation trading (Banderet) projects Eurozone core inflation averaging 2.9% next year and headline reaching 4.4%. It sees the December holiday period and Q1 2027 as turning points as costs broaden to processed food, services contract resets and non-energy industrial goods, and says the market is too complacent.

On data-centre policy, GS political and sector analysts expect Democratic governors in Texas, Georgia and Michigan to impose conditional moratoria. States likely to restrict account for roughly 45% of planned US data-centre capacity, with Texas alone about 25%. The consensus within GS is that this is a risk to timing rather than to capacity, since the extra costs are marginal relative to build cost and some hyperscalers have already accepted the terms.

The core trade thesis is opportunistic value in beaten-up cyclical assets into year-end. The reasoning is lower odds of a major Gulf escalation after the mid-terms (oil $85-105 with downside asymmetry), data-centre capex still being executed, very light risk appetite after heavy de-grossing, and robust US and global growth.

Funding recommendation: the case for funding via USD has eroded with sequential Fed hikes on the table and an uncertain terminal rate. GS prefers EUR (or CHF) funding for high-beta and pro-risk longs, citing recent position reduction and French political and fiscal risk into year-end. Franchise favourites are AUD, GBP, ZAR and MXN.

FX trade expressions are 3m dual binaries on EURUSD < 1.1100 (already in the money) versus USDZAR < 16.60 for 7.50% (~13.25x leverage) and versus USDMXN < 18.15 for 9.50% (~10.5x leverage). Max loss is the premium spent.

EM rates trades are to receive HUF 5y5y on a move to 5.00% (last 4.90%, target 4.50%, unlimited max loss) and to buy SAGB R2037 at 8.80% and above (last 8.75%, target 8.25%). The desk notes these are the only two markets in the region with positioning, so it advises averaging in and being careful on timing because of Fed-led dollar strength risk.

GS STS strategies are long FX/EMFX carry (GSFXCAM0 Index) and long Brent vol relative value via front-to-back expiries (GSVLBRR5 Index). The Brent trade sells 1m ATM straddles and buys 6m OTM strangles, since realised moves have not justified implied breakevens and the 1m vs 6m term structure sits at 11 vols of backwardation.

Equity-FX trade: sell EURUSD versus SPX/NDX correlation at +15% implied, since realised correlation has been very negative at times over the last 2 years. Expressed through Feb27 dual binaries on SPX > 105.5% or NDX > 108.5% versus EURUSD < 1.10 for 10% USD (~10x leverage).

Brazil: positioning is light and the mood is defensive. The fiscal package failed to impress the market, and macro sales calls Brazil cheap but at risk of being a value trap. The rates desk favours front-end receivers, NTN-B real-rate receivers (2028-2030) and DI steepeners. FX trading is tactically buying USDBRL dips, with 5.70/5.80 a possible entry area.

EWZ is down 23% since the election while EEM and ACWI are roughly flat. Only about half of the pre-election inflows have left, leaving about US$1.5bn still to be sold at about US$150mn a day in redemptions, with a cleaner position by mid-December. Volumes have fallen from US$15bn to US$5bn a day, so the exit is narrowing.

tension_points.bull_case: Korapaty puts the end of the current adjustment at 4.25-4.5%, and Xholi says the 4.75% market-implied peak is above where the Committee ends up and driven by positioning, so he buys U7.
tension_points.bear_case: Bingham sees upside policy risks into the December SEP, front-loaded 2027 hikes and terminal pricing that reacts violently to any wobble in AI sentiment, while GS Economics now expects a third hike in March.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further hot core inflation reports without progress, which GS Economics says could bring a January hike.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers have begun agreeing to the Texas conditions, added costs are marginal relative to build cost, and demand is very strong, so the risk is to timing rather than capacity.
tension_points.bear_case: Conditional moratoria in Texas, Georgia and Michigan, tax-break repeal and tighter water and power rules affect states with about 45% of planned US capacity.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Texas legislation in 2027 that adds binding protections and a pause on new permits that outlasts the legislative process.

tension_points.bull_case: If shelter reverts to its baseline trend, the risk of material reinflation in 2027 stays muted, and the noisy CPI components printed to the downside.
tension_points.bear_case: Lavenberg and Cahill see broad-based small upside beats and pipeline pressure, and Banderet sees the market as too complacent.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A move toward a 30bps MoM OER run rate versus 20bps, which would put a floor under inflation heading into the start-of-2027 annual price resets.

tension_points.bull_case: Brazil looks cheap, with light positioning and USDBRL dips seen as potential entry points on year-end seasonality and carry.
tension_points.bear_case: Macro sales calls it a possible value trap with a defensive investor base, a weak fiscal package, a hawkish Fed and about US$1.5bn of EWZ still to be sold.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A credible Finance Minister and central bank appointments plus external help from a weaker dollar and lower oil would support a re-rating.
